arguments.command:
termy_say -s "Generating timing entropy" &&
printf "\r\nResult: " &&
flips="" &&
while [ ${#flips} -lt 256 ]; do
 coin=0 &&
 t=$(date +%s%N) &&
 t=$((t + 1000000)) &&
 while [ $(date +%s%N) -lt $t ]; do
  coin=$((coin ^ 1))
 done &&
 flips="${flips}${coin}"
done &&
echo "$flips" |
sha256sum |
awk '{print $1}' &&
printf ""
arguments.explanation: Generates a 256-bit entropy string using nanosecond clock drift loops compatible with Bash and Zsh, hashes it with sha256sum, and outputs the random string.
arguments.goal: Generate a secure random hash using timing drift entropy

arguments.command:
termy_say -s "Please enter the domain name" &&
printf "\r\n🔒 Domain name: " &&
read -r domain &&
if [ -n "$domain" ]; then
 CERT_DATA=$(echo | openssl s_client -connect "$domain:443" -servername "$domain" 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -enddate 2>/dev/null | cut -d= -f2) &&
 if [ -n "$CERT_DATA" ]; then
  printf "\n📜 SSL Expiration Date: \033[1m%s\033[22m\n" "$CERT_DATA" &&
  termy_say -s "The S S L certificate expires on $CERT_DATA";
 else
  printf "\n⛔ Could not retrieve SSL certificate for that domain.\n" &&
  termy_say -s "Connection failed";
 fi;
else
 printf "\n⛔ Domain cannot be empty.\n" &&
 termy_say -s "Operation cancelled";
fi
arguments.explanation: Checks the SSL certificate expiration date of a domain and speaks the result.

 port=${port:-4444} &&

 printf "\r\n🎧 Server active on port $port. Waiting...\n" &&
